cohort: 260 women on the postnatal ward of an academic hospital in Tehran, Iran, during the COVID-19 pandemic (March-August 2021)
finding: Women with a history of COVID-19 infection during pregnancy had a lower rate of exclusive breastfeeding at 8 weeks postpartum compared to women without COVID-19 infection.
mod_finding: The study found that women with a history of COVID-19 infection had a higher prevalence of cesarean section and were less likely to successfully exclusively breastfeed compared to those without a history of COVID-19 infection.
gest_age: Mean infant gestational age was lower in the COVID-19 infection group (P < 0.001)
